question: ________ is a process in which two close-fitting parts are joined by using a filler material which is heated above its melting point and distributed in the gap by capillary action.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Brazing.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Brazing** is the process in which** two close-fitting parts** are joined by using a **filler material** which is **heated above its melting point **and distributed in the gap by capillary action.
 
• **Hardening:** This option is** incorrect **as it does not involve joining two parts using a filler material.
 
• **Soldering:** This option is** incorrect **as it involves joining two parts using a filler material but the filler material is not heated above its melting point.
 
• **Welding: **This option is **incorrect **as it involves joining two parts by melting the surfaces of the parts and not by using a filler material.
 
• Therefore, the **correct** answer is option 4, Brazing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hardening:** It is a process of making a **metal harder** by** heating it** and then **cooling it rapidly.**
 
• **Soldering:** It is a process in which two or more metal items are** joined **together by** melting and flowing a filler metal **into the joint.
 
• **Welding:** It is a process of** joining two or more metal parts** by heating the surfaces to their **melting point **and joining them together.
